The HN tensile fracture had a crater shape with larger, deeper and more uniformly distributed dimples than LN; the HN impact fracture showed larger, deeper and more uniform dimples with a higher shear-lip area ratio.
Aggregated AlN inclusions were detected in the dimples of the HN steel; they were generated during the smelting process and tended to cause crack initiation (detrimental to mechanical properties).

AlN stability diagram: the HN composition (Al 9.95 wt%, N 0.1326 wt%) lies far above the equilibrium AlN line at the smelting temperature (1873 K), so AlN inclusions can be easily formed and stably exist during smelting.
